```{r}
library('ggplot2')
library('purrr')
library('dplyr')
library('gtsummary')
library('gt')
```

```{r}
# Self-contained synthetic data: this example ships with the public package
# and must not depend on any private data source.
set.seed(42)
n <- 60
input_parameters_raw <- tibble::tibble(
  subject_id = sprintf("SUBJ-%03d", seq_len(n)),
  treatment_group = sample(c("Control", "Treatment"), n, replace = TRUE),
  site = sample(c("Hospital A", "Hospital B", "Clinic C"), n, replace = TRUE),
  baseline_sbp = round(rnorm(n, mean = 130, sd = 10), 1),
  followup_sbp = round(rnorm(n, mean = 122, sd = 12), 1),
  biomarker_a = round(rgamma(n, shape = 4, rate = 1), 2),
  biomarker_b = round(biomarker_a + rgamma(n, shape = 2, rate = 1), 2),
  duration_days = round(rgamma(n, shape = 6, rate = 0.8), 2),
  cholesterol_mg_dl = round(rgamma(n, shape = 5, rate = 1.2), 2),
  adverse_event_1 = sample(c(0, 1), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.7, 0.3)),
  adverse_event_2 = sample(c(0, 1), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.85, 0.15)),
  adverse_event_3 = sample(c(0, 1), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.6, 0.4))
)
```

# Quarto Example 

This is an example of an Rmarkdown. This package comes with several common R packages, it is also recommended to install:  

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c('gt', # general table formatting
                   'gtsummary', # for univariate and regression tables
                   'here', # where you are working (better when working with git)
                   'knitr', # r package for working with documents 
                   'quarto', # R package for working with quarto 
                   'rmarkdown', # creating documents
                   'tidymodels', # modern interface for fitting models 
                   'tidyverse', # modern R language 
                   'tinytex', # needed for pdf documents 
                   'devtools' # package creation development tools
                   ))


remotes::install_github("Pakillo/grateful") # for package citation
```

To create pdf documents it is also recommended to run

```{r, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```

```{r knitr-example, tab.cap="first 5 records and 5 columns of the data"}
input_parameters_raw %>%
  head(n = 5) %>%
  select(subject_id, treatment_group, site, baseline_sbp, followup_sbp) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

# Table One

```{r table1, tab.cap="An example of a Table 1"}
input_parameters_raw %>%
  select(-subject_id, -adverse_event_1, -adverse_event_2, -adverse_event_3) %>%
  tbl_summary(by = "treatment_group",
              type = all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
              statistic = list(
                all_continuous() ~ c("{mean} ({sd})","{median} ({p25}, {p75})","{median} ({min} - {max})")
                )
  ) %>%
  add_p(pvalue_fun = ~ style_pvalue(.x, digits = 2)) %>%
  add_overall(last = TRUE, col_label = "**Overall**") %>%
  separate_p_footnotes() %>% 
  as_gt() %>%
  gt::as_latex() # for pdf documents 
```


# Cross Refrence 
You can cross-reference tables, listings, figures and page numbers 

You can use the `label`s you created to reference the tables like \@ref(tab:table1) or items in the `bib.bib` file such as @Al-Helali2021-as. 

You can even reference later figures such as \@ref(fig:fig-2) or sections like \@ref(sec:software) or even the page number that something happens on \pageref{fig:fig-3}.


# Pairwise t-tests

Suppose we wanted to visualize all pairwise t-tests (we will only do first four but you get the idea). There are other ways to do this but this is a good enough example of repeated analysis. 


```{r}
features_numeric <- input_parameters_raw %>%
  select(-subject_id) %>%
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  colnames()


pairs <- combn(features_numeric,2) |> 
  t() %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(pair_number = row_number()) 

pair_number_list <- pairs %>% filter(pair_number <= 4) %>% pull(pair_number)
```


```{r, label='t_test_child', results='asis'}
if(!interactive()){
  src <- lapply(pair_number_list,
                function(pair_number){knitr::knit_expand('t_test_child.Rmd')})
  res = knitr::knit_child(text = unlist(src), quiet = TRUE)
  cat(res, sep = '\n')
}
```
